source.title: Syzygies of projective varieties of large degree: recent progress and open problems.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth complex projective variety of dimension n, let A be an ample divisor on X, let P be an arbitrary divisor, let B be a fixed twisting divisor, and set L_d = dA + P. For a fixed weight q with 2 <= q <= n, does there exist a constant C3 depending on X, A, B, and P such that the Koszul cohomology group K_{p,q}(X,B;L_d) vanishes for every p <= C3 d^(q-1) once d is sufficiently large? In other words, is the lower bound in the asymptotic non-vanishing theorem sharp up to a constant in the sense that all lower-index weight-q syzygies eventually disappear?

evidence.quote: Returning to the situation of Theorem 1.8, it is natural to ask what happens for those values of p outside the range governed by the statement. We conjecture that the lower bound appearing in (1.1) is actually the best possible in the sense that one has vanishing of pth syzygies for smaller p.
Conjecture 1.10. (Asymptotic vanishing). Fix q ∈ [2,n ]. In the situation of Theorem 1.8, there is a constant C3 (depending on X, A,B and P ) such that Kp,q(X,B :Ld) = 0 for p ≤ C3 ·dq−1 when d ≫ 0.
We consider the Conjecture to be the main open problem concerning the rough asymptotics of the Kp,q.

accepted.question_text: For projective space P^n, integers b and d, and the Veronese syzygy groups K_{p,q}(n,b;d) = K_{p,q}(P^n, O_{P^n}(b); O_{P^n}(d)), is the non-vanishing range proved in Theorem 2.1 exact? Equivalently, do all groups K_{p,q}(n,b;d) vanish whenever p lies outside the range predicted by that theorem?
accepted.context_brief: sharp vanishing range for Veronese syzygies

evidence.quote: We believe that the Theorem actually gives the precise non-vanishing range for Veronese syzygies:
Conjecture 2.3. In the situation of the Theorem, one has Kp,q(n,b ;d) = 0 when p lies outside the range (∗).
This provides at least some evidence for Conjectures 2.3 and 1.10.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth projective variety of dimension n, fix a weight q with 1 <= q <= n, and let L_d be a sufficiently positive line bundle as in the paper. Do there exist normalizing functions F_q(d), depending on X and the geometric data, such that the Betti numbers k_{p_d,q}(X;L_d) become asymptotically Gaussian after normalization, namely F_q(d) · k_{p_d,q}(X;L_d) -> e^(-a^2/2) whenever p_d approaches r_d/2 + a·sqrt(r_d)/2 as d -> infinity? The source also asks for the analogous behavior for the twisted groups k_{p,q}(X,B;L_d).

evidence.quote: We conjectue that the same pattern holds universally:

Conjecture 3.2. Returning to a smooth projective variety X of dimension n, ﬁx q ∈ [1,n ]. Then there is a normalizing function Fq(d) (depending on X and geometric data) such that Fq(d) ·kpd,q(X;Ld) − →e−a2/2 as d → ∞ and pd → rd / 2 + a · √rd / 2 .
One expects slightly more generally that the analogous statement is true for the dimensions kp,q(X,B ;Ld) with B a ﬁxed twisting line bundle.

accepted.question_text: In the asymptotic Boij-Soderberg decomposition for the syzygies under discussion, especially for the coefficients x_i(P^2,B;L_d), can one normalize both the coefficients and the relevant indices i so that, as d tends to infinity, they are sampled values of a smooth function on a dense subset of its domain? The same source notes that one would also like an analogous formulation in dimensions n >= 3, although the appropriate Boij-Soderberg data are then less canonical.

evidence.quote: Remark 3.4. (Asymptotic Boij-S¨ oderberg coeﬃcients). Returning to the global situation, we ask the following

Question. Can one normalize the Boij-S¨ oderberg coeﬃcientsxi(P2,B ;Ld) and the relevant values of i in such a way that as d → ∞ they arise as the values of a smooth function deﬁned on a dense set in its domain?
Of course one would like to ask the same question also in dimensions n ≥ 3, but here there is some ambiguity in chosing Boij-S¨ oderberg data.

accepted.question_text: Let C be a smooth projective curve, let B be a line bundle on C, and let L_d be a line bundle of sufficiently large degree. For exactly which integers p is the weight-one Koszul cohomology group K_{p,1}(C,B;L_d) nonzero? The source later answers this by showing that K_{p,1}(C,B;L_d) vanishes for all sufficiently large d if and only if B is p-very ample, which resolves the question in the source artifact.
accepted.context_brief: weight-one curve syzygies for large degree

evidence.quote: However this leaves open the Question 4.1. For which values of p is Kp,1(C,B ;Ld) ̸= 0 when d ≫ 0?
Theorem 4.3. Fix a line bundle B on C. Then Kp,1(C,B ;Ld) = 0 for d ≫ 0 if and only if B is p-very ample.

accepted.question_text: For a smooth projective curve C with gonality gon(C), and for a sufficiently positive line bundle L_d on C, is the Koszul cohomology group K_{p,1}(C,K_C;L_d) nonzero exactly for those p with gon(C) <= p + 1? The source explicitly states this gonality conjecture and then states that it follows from Theorem 4.3, so within this source artifact it is presented as resolved.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.2. Ford ≫ 0, Kp,1(C,KC;Ld) ̸= 0 ⇐ ⇒ gon(C) ≤ p + 1.
It follows from Riemann–Roch that the canonical bundle KC fails to be p-very ample if and only if gon(C) ≤ p + 1. Therefore Conjecture 4.2 is a consequence of Theorem 4.3.
Thus for example Conjecture 4.2 holds for any line bundle Ld of degree d ≥ 4g − 3.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth projective variety of dimension at least 2, let B be a line bundle on X, and let L_d be sufficiently positive. Find necessary and sufficient conditions for the vanishing of K_{p,1}(X,B;L_d) for all large d. In particular, determine whether failure of p-jet very ampleness should force non-vanishing, or whether a subtler condition involving smoothable zero-dimensional subschemes is required.

evidence.quote: To complete this picture, there remains:
Problem 4.12. Find necessary and suﬃcient conditions for the vanishing ofKp,1(X,B ;Ld) when d ≫ 0.

It does not seem out of the question that the failure of B to be p-jet very ample in general implies the non-vanishing of this group. We had originally imagined the p-very amplitude ofB would control the matter, but a heuristic argument due to Yang casts some doubt on this possibility.
